title: Biobanks and Population Genomic Research
summary: All of Us, UK Biobank, Million Veteran Program — large-scale genomic cohorts reshaping discovery.

content_blocks.text: Individual genomic tests generate clinical insights for one patient. Population-scale biobanks — linking genomic data to longitudinal health records for hundreds of thousands to millions of individuals — generate discovery insights that reshape guidelines for everyone. Several landmark biobanks are now producing clinical-grade evidence across diverse populations.

content_blocks.text: Phenome-Wide Association Studies (PheWAS) flip the GWAS paradigm: instead of testing one SNP against one disease, PheWAS tests one genetic variant against hundreds of disease phenotypes extracted from EHR ICD codes. This approach has revealed unexpected pleiotropic effects — variants affecting multiple organ systems — and repurposed drugs by identifying shared genetic architecture across diseases.

content_blocks.body: Polygenic Risk Scores (PRS) aggregate thousands of common variants, each with small effect, into a composite genomic risk score for complex diseases (coronary artery disease, type 2 diabetes, breast cancer). Individuals in the top 10% of PRS for CAD have a 3-fold elevated lifetime risk — comparable to rare Mendelian variants. PRS are beginning to enter clinical guidance for statin initiation and mammography scheduling.
